thread:
maya: Quick post-all-hands follow-up: customers want a concise summary of regional prewarm behavior, SLA scope during fallthroughs, and who can trigger on-demand prewarm. Can we put this in a short comms blurb?
chris: TL;DR: prewarm triggers automatically from short-term forecasts or manually via reserve. Routing fallthrough order is: in-region Dedicated -> in-region Hosted burst -> nearest-region Dedicated -> nearest-region Hosted -> preemptible/spot. SLA covers in-region Dedicated and pinned Hosted only. Latency expectations: typical nearby-region +30-150ms, intercontinental +200-400ms; we'll publish p50/p90/p99 soon. Billing: customers pay for tokens consumed as usual; no extra SLA credits for fallthroughs.
anika: Prewarm details: we start warm workers ~90s before accept traffic; KV prefix cache and full steady throughput often need 3-5min to fully prime. So expect degraded throughput for the first few minutes after spill.
ops-bot: autoscaler: promoted autoscale-policy-v1.15 to canary at 08:12 UTC monitoring enabled.
tom: Ops question: can oncall trigger on-demand prewarm? Who has authority to commit extra capacity?
chris: Oncall can kick a one-off prewarm via the runbook UI for up to 1h. Any commit >1h or that increases reserved Dedicated capacity requires infra lead approval. We'll add a quick-approve button to the canary panel.
zara: Any mitigation for noisy neighbors during bursts? Small customers hit SLOs yesterday.
sylvie: We're testing a soft tenant-cap + gradual slowdown knob in canary (it reduces max concurrency for heavy tenants rather than hard kill). It should protect small tenants while allowing large ones to be throttled gracefully.
maya: Action items: chris to draft external blurb + p50/p90/p99 table by Tue EOD; anika to add warmup-time note to infra docs; sylvie to surface tenant-cap toggle in canary UI; tom to update runbook with oncall prewarm steps. I'll collect PR links and share in infra channel.
